title: A prime-scale truncated Gaussian keeps its separator corner positive (no new κ)
body:
## Summary
- At `p=19`, `theta=1/1444`, `alpha=3`, and `gamma=9*pi*1445/1444`, the centered bandwidth-2 truncation keeps a positive Schur corner between vertices 1 and 8, strictly between `1/10^136` and `1/10^135`. The half-bandwidth in survivor order is 3.
- The parameter sandwich `4 log(304) <= 9 pi <= 5 log(304)` is proved at this prime. The truncation's off-diagonal row sum is below `1/10^11`. That does not check the note's tail bound `exp(-2 a theta)+5 exp(-2a)`.
- No new kappa is claimed. The selected record is unchanged. This is one prime and width 2, not the all-size bandwidth claim.

## Test plan
